summary.headline: INDO SMC guided FY27 revenue to INR450-500 crores on an INR237 crore order book plus INR125 crore fresh orders, with margins targeted at 15%+.
summary.overview: FY26 was the first full year after listing, with management saying revenue roughly doubled and PAT more than doubled, driven by higher-value CT/PT, bus duct, meter cubicle and panel products. Management attributed a softer March-quarter SMC and FRP output to geopolitics-driven resin and petroleum-product price swings and supply gaps. The company shifted to shorter (2-3 month) orders with price-escalation clauses (5% trigger) and said it is now choosing orders on margin. Inventory rose to about INR85 crores (around 100 days) because of pre-stocked raw materials, and the working capital cycle was cut from 83 to about 40 days. Management did not give a precise FY26 revenue or margin figure in the call; the 15% EBITDA margin cited by analysts was not confirmed by management.

financial_highlights.metric: Fresh orders from April 1 to call date (as cited by management)
Combined order book (per management, including fresh orders)
EBITDA margin (as cited by analyst, not confirmed by management)

segments.name: CT/PT and LTCT (instrument transformers, electrical engineering)
segments.commentary: About INR120-125 crores of the order book; management said CT/PT is more engineering-intensive with margins above SMC/FRP, targeting above 18% EBITDA on standardised products. Currently operating at 11 kV and 33 kV, with 66 kV and above still in planning.

segments.name: Bus ducts, meter cubicles and panels
segments.commentary: Meter cubicle orders of INR10-15 crores were added, with new meter cubicle orders of INR10 crores-plus taken in the current period. Management described these as higher-margin lines bundled with SMC and CT/PT.

segments.name: SMC
segments.commentary: About INR80 crores of order book being executed month to month. Management said FY26 SMC and FRP output fell in March due to resin and petroleum-product shortages; the call did not give segment revenue figures.

segments.name: FRP (pultrusion, gratings) and tarpaulin
segments.commentary: Remainder of the order book, executed against monthly clearances. Plan to add about 300 tons of FRP production capacity.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Early-stage: Oman and Gulf orders, samples sent to US and Germany, Dubai electrical fair planned from September. Management said UL 94 certification is a requirement for the US and that certification takes 1-2 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR450-500 crores, subject to geopolitics and material availability; management said it can be met with existing capacity plus automation machinery.
H1 FY27 inflow target of INR200 crores-plus, lowered from an earlier INR250 crores-plus; management said H2 is expected to be stronger than H1.
EBITDA margin target of 15% or above; management said it expects to maintain FY26 margins in FY27 and aims for 1-2% better if conditions allow.
Medium-term aim of INR1,000 crores-plus revenue in about three years, with railways a major contributor from FY28 onward.
Railway clearance expected by end of the following month after the call, pending lab expansion; management said trial orders would grow over the next three years.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR25 crores (as disclosed in the IPO) is the first priority, covering machines and facilities across SMC, FRP and electrical engineering.
A 2,000-ton-plus SMC press is expected in 2-3 months, to enable larger railway products and big boxes; SMC capacity target is 6,000 tons-plus.
Nashik (Maharashtra) plant needs capex and more space; a second plant at Nashik has started production readiness. Ahmedabad is running well on utilisation.
Management said revenue above INR750 crores could come from the full capex once complete, and the company has land available so no major new building is needed.
Plans for 33 kV CTs and meter cubicles; a lab expansion funded from the IPO is expected to be completed by the end of the month after the call.
demand_pricing: Management said the utilities and electrical industry (SMC, FRP, CT/PT, LTCT, bus ducts, switchgear) is growing fast; it cited about 20 states served and a push to expand pan-India and export.
Pricing: management said recent orders are priced around INR450 per unit versus INR350-360 earlier, and that buyers are accepting the higher prices.
Competition in higher-kV CT/PT is limited: management said few players hold approvals, and cited ABB Crompton as operating at 66, 120 and 240 kV.

Raw materials: resin (SMC/FRP) and petroleum-linked inputs were the main pressure; glass fiber held in about 3 months' stock; copper and steel costs passed through at order time. Management said it took a hit on resin in March.
Order inflow pace: management cited INR3-4 crores in new orders on the day of the call and said small orders are taken to limit price-risk exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SMC and FRP fall while CT/PT rose, and what is the order book breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SMC and FRP fell from March due to geopolitics-driven resin and petroleum shortages and rate swings. Order book: about INR125 crores in CT/PT and LTCT, about INR80 crores in SMC, and the rest in FRP and tarpaulin.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins rise above 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15%-plus is the target and the margin is sustainable, with the company now choosing higher-margin orders and CT/PT expected to earn above 18% on standardised products.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be funded, and will there be dilution or debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the working cycle improvement plus IPO cash should avoid a funding need this year; any future funding would be decided after September based on six-month results, with debt or equity depending on order size.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it began exports to Oman and the Gulf, sent samples to the US and Germany, plans to attend a Dubai electrical fair from September, and needs client approvals that take 1-2 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company reach INR1,000 crores revenue, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets INR1,000-plus crores in about three years, with railways contributing a significant share from FY28.

risks_watch: Resin and petroleum-product availability and price swings; management says price-escalation clauses apply only when moves exceed 5%.
Working capital: inventory at about INR85 crores (about 100 days) and the stated need to keep the cycle at 40-45 days.
Railway approvals delayed beyond the March expectation; management now expects clearance about a month after the call.
H1 FY27 inflow target cut to INR200 crores-plus from INR250 crores-plus; management did not give a full-year order inflow figure.
Dependence on government and utility orders; CRGO cores are imported from Korea, China, Japan and Taiwan.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and margins, but cautious and hedged on near-term execution, citing geopolitics and material costs repeatedly. Several answers were vague or repeated, and some figures (order book breakup, 15% margin) were restated by analysts rather than confirmed by management.
key_quotes: Our target for this year is to achieve INR450 crores plus, and we are focused on that.
Yes, it is sustainable. We want to work at this minimum level and will target even better margins.
But standardized we will almost want to work above 18% EBITDA.
